title: Anisotropic noise contracts moments
statement: Let $[?]$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $[?]$, and let a finite nonempty index set label an orthonormal basis of real functions on that set containing the constant-one function. For a positive integer $n$, choose real noise parameters $\rho_i\in[0,1]$ for each coordinate, and let $T_\rho f$ be the Fourier operator that multiplies each product-basis coefficient by the product of the $[?]$ over coordinates where its basis index is nonconstant. Then for every real-valued function $f$ on $[?]^n$ and every real $p\geq1$, the product-measure mean of $|T_\rho f|^p$ is at most the product-measure mean of $|f|^p$.
